The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Product or Service Development activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all otheractivities).Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR200,000. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industryandwould lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. GSTP Element 2 "Make" aims to support design, development, and demonstration activities. Products and technologies are defined to be any hardware, software, or applications within the scope set out in section 3 below. Key characteristics of this Element are:  The role of industry in defining and proposing projects oriented to commercial or institutional opportunities in all areas of satellite applications except satellite telecommunication (not covered by GSTP);  The outcome of an activity will eventually become a product ready for exploitation.  The sharing of funding by ESA and industry. Activities submitted in the frame of GSTP Element 2 Make" may be related to the improvement or development of satellite subsystems or equipment (including EGSE), space transportation subsystems or equipment up to engineering model or qualification model, and the improvement or development of ground / user system and equipment up to prototypes and commercialized products. Activities should address any the following technology themes: Earth observation, science, exploration, human spaceflight, space transportation, satellite navigation or generic technologies.
